column3: The Hebrew has transgression and sin in the singular; BSB has transgressions and sins.
The Hebrew says for I kept silent and describes roaring all day; BSB says when and groaning.
The Hebrew names sap and its transformation; BSB speaks of strength being drained.
The Hebrew’s first verb is uncompleted, while BSB says I acknowledged. Forgiveness is pictured as carrying away guilt.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name You as the one found and has him as the object the waters do not reach.
The Hebrew explicitly names my eye over you; BSB says watch over you.
The Hebrew ends with not drawing near to you; BSB makes making them come to you the purpose of control.
